This former army chief seized power in a 2014 coup, installed a military junta, and went on to serve as Thailand's prime minister for nearly a decade. Who is he?
Prayut Chan-o-cha: Prime Minister of Thailand from 2014 to 2023.

Serving as India's president from 2017 to 2022, he was the first person from Uttar Pradesh and the first member of the Bharatiya Janata Party to hold that office, after serving as Governor of Bihar — who is he?
Ram Nath Kovind: President of India from 2017 to 2022.

Fought from 1921 to 1926, this conflict pitted Spain and later France against Berber guerrillas led by Abd el-Krim in northern Morocco, and saw history's first amphibious landing to use tanks and aircraft — which conflict?
Rif War: 1921–1926 war between Spain and Riffian tribes of Morocco.
Founded by a Varangian prince who settled at Novgorod in 862, this noble lineage ruled Kievan Rus' and, through its Moscow branch, the tsars of Russia until 1598 — what dynasty was it?
Rurikids: Noble lineage and rulers of Kievan Rus'. The Rurikids were the ruling dynasty of Kievan Rus' and its principalities following its disintegration.
After leaving office, she traded the Finnish prime minister's chair for a desk at the Tony Blair Institute, advising on leadership reform — which young Social Democrat was she?
Sanna Marin: Prime Minister of Finland from 2019 to 2023.
A veteran of the Soviet-Afghan and Chechen wars, this Russian air-force chief was reportedly sacked by Putin over ties to the Wagner Group rebellion — who is he?
Existing from 57 BCE to 935 CE and forming the Three Kingdoms of Korea alongside Paekche and Goguryeo, which kingdom had the smallest population of the three?
Silla: Korean kingdom (57 BCE–935 CE). Silla was one of the longest-lasting countries in Korean history.
This leading man of 1950s Westerns and film noir later played General Jack D. Ripper in Dr. Strangelove and Captain McCluskey in The Godfather — who is he?

Punished in the underworld by standing in a pool beneath a fruit tree whose branches always pulled away from his grasp, this Greek mythological figure lent his name to the English word for teasing someone with something unreachable — who was he?
Tantalus: Greek mythological figure and son of Zeus.
This Norwegian adventurer drifted 8,000 km across the Pacific on a hand-built raft in 1947 to test his theory that South Americans settled Polynesia first — who is he?
Thor Heyerdahl: Norwegian anthropologist and adventurer (1914–2002)
This Indian revolutionary assassinated the former Punjab lieutenant governor in 1940 in revenge for the 1919 Jallianwala Bagh massacre, of which he was a survivor — who was he?
Udham Singh: Indian revolutionary (1899–1940). Singh was subsequently tried and convicted of murder and hanged in July 1940.
In 1976, this Soviet pilot defected to the West by flying his MiG-25 'Foxbat' jet interceptor to Japan, handing the CIA what George H. W. Bush called an 'intelligence bonanza' — who is he?
Viktor Belenko: Soviet pilot who defected to the West (1947–2023)

Beginning with the 1916 death of Yuan Shikai, this chaotic decade-plus in Chinese history saw the country splinter under rival military cliques until Sun Yat-sen's Nationalists challenged the Beijing government for legitimacy — which period?
Warlord Era: Period in the history of the Republic of China (1916–1928)

Convinced that Protestants and the Catholic majority had to make common cause against the Crown, this revolutionary helped found the Society of United Irishmen in 1791 and became an icon of Irish republicanism — who was he?
A career Army general who became a national hero in the Mexican-American War, this 12th U.S. president died of a stomach illness just 16 months into office — who is he?
Zachary Taylor: President of the United States from 1849 to 1850.
Which of these people was born first?
Ada Lovelace (born 1815) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these was born first?
Benjamin Banneker (born 1731) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was born first?
Christine Ladd-Franklin (born 1847) is the earliest of the four. Christine Ladd-Franklin (December 1, 1847 – March 5, 1930) was an American psychologist, logician, and mathematician.
Which one below was established earliest?
Bash (Unix shell) (founded 1989) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the oldest release?
Pascal (programming language) (published 1972) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Rosalyn Sussman Yalow is a physicist.
Which of these is a chemist?
Jan Baptist van Helmont is a chemist.
What is the atomic number of Carbon?
Carbon (from Latin carbo 'coal') is a chemical element; it has symbol C and atomic number 6.
In what year was J. Robert Oppenheimer born?
J. Robert Oppenheimer: In 1941, Oppenheimer was briefed about nuclear weapon design by Australian physicist Mark Oliphant.
In what year was Arthur Conan Doyle born?
Arthur Conan Doyle: Sir Arthur Ignatius Conan Doyle (22 May 1859 – 7 July 1930) was a British writer and physician.
In what year was José M. Hernández born?
José M. Hernández: José Moreno Hernández (born August 7, 1962) is a Mexican-American engineer and astronaut.
In what year did Jean Tatlock die?
Jean Tatlock: Jean Frances Tatlock (February 21, 1914 – January 4, 1944) was an American psychiatrist.
In what year did Anton Chekhov die?
Anton Chekhov: Along with Henrik Ibsen and August Strindberg, Chekhov is often referred to as one of the three seminal figures in the birth of early modernism in the theatre.
In what year was Factitious disorder imposed on another discovered?
Factitious disorder imposed on another: The victim is typically the caregiver's child but is occasionally an adult partner.
In what year was Iridium discovered?
Iridium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ir and atomic number 77.
China Banknote Printing and Minting Corporation
Ondansetron: Pfizer. It is also effective for treating gastroenteritis.
In which country is Minamata disease?
Minamata disease: Japan. Minamata disease (Japanese: 水俣病, Hepburn: Minamata-byō) is a neurological disease caused by severe mercury poisoning.
Who is credited with discovering Caesium?
Caesium: Robert Bunsen. Caesium (IUPAC spelling; also spelled cesium in American English) is a chemical element; it has symbol Cs and atomic number 55.
Who is credited with discovering Nobelium?
Nobelium: Glenn Theodore Seaborg. Nobelium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol No and atomic number 102.
Who is credited with discovering Silicon?
Silicon: Jöns Jacob Berzelius. Silicon (SILL-ih-kən) is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
This disorder caused by excess growth hormone after the growth plates close typically first shows up as enlarged hands and feet, followed by a bigger forehead, jaw, and nose — what is it?
Acromegaly is a disorder that results in excess growth of certain parts of the human body.
Often caused by misaligned or unevenly focused eyes in early childhood, this is the most common cause of single-eye vision loss in kids and young adults, nicknamed 'lazy eye' — what condition is it?
Amblyopia is a disorder of sight in which the brain fails to fully process input from one eye and over time favors the other eye.
It can't touch a virus or a fungus, but a few varieties even fight protozoa — this class of drug is the frontline weapon against bacterial infection; what is it?
Antibiotic is a type of antimicrobial substance active against bacteria.

Distinguished from celestial mechanics by asking what heavenly bodies ARE rather than where they are, this science applies physics and chemistry to the Sun, stars, galaxies, and exoplanets — which discipline?
Astrophysics is a science that applies the methods and principles of physics and chemistry in the study of astronomical objects and phenomena including the universe.
Strawberries, blackcurrants and blueberries all count in the kitchen sense — though botanists would object, since the culinary meaning of this word differs from the scientific one. What word?
Berry is a small, pulpy, and often edible fruit.
Caused by a toxin that thrives in low-oxygen conditions — the same one sold cosmetically as 'botox' — this rare illness brings blurred vision and creeping paralysis but rarely a fever. What is it?
Botulism is a rare and potentially fatal illness caused by botulinum toxin (commonly referred to as botox), which is produced by the bacterium Clostridium botulinum.

The largest land bird in North America went fully extinct in the wild in 1987 when every survivor was captured for breeding — which critically endangered vulture has since returned to the Grand Canyon and beyond?
California condor (Gymnogyps californianus) is a New World vulture and the largest North American land bird.
This worldwide family of over 5,000 fly species — found everywhere except the Antarctic and Arctic — includes the biting midges also known as sand flies — what is it called?
Ceratopogonidae is a family of flies colloquially known as no-see-ums, sand flies, or biting midges, generally 1-3 millimetres (116-18 in) in length.
An American naturalist who surveyed wildlife in Labrador, he turned what he learned there into quick-freezing methods that launched the modern frozen-food industry. Who was he?
Clarence Birdseye (December 9, 1886 - October 7, 1956) was an American inventor, entrepreneur, and naturalist, who is widely considered the founder of the modern frozen food industry.
Thanks to variations in the OR6A2 gene, some people taste this Mediterranean herb as fresh and citrusy while others swear it tastes like soap — its leaves are called cilantro in the US. What is it?
Coriander is an annual herb in the family Apiaceae.

This American nuclear physicist worked on the Manhattan Project and later led the Federation of American Scientists, best remembered for his 1959 testimony that helped sink a controversial cabinet nomination — who is he?
David L. Hill (November 11, 1919 - December 14, 2008) was an American nuclear physicist who worked on the Manhattan Project during World War II and was head of the Federation of American Scientists.
This waterfowl belongs to the same family as swans and geese, but is generally smaller and shorter-necked — and despite the shared family, swans and geese don't count as one. What is it?
Duck is the common name for numerous species of waterfowl in the family Anatidae.

Named for Latin words meaning 'within the cytoplasm' and 'little net,' this eukaryotic cell organelle handles protein folding and comes in rough and smooth varieties, forming an interconnected network of membrane-enclosed sacs — name this organelle?
Endoplasmic reticulum (ER) is a part of a transportation system of the eukaryotic cell, and has many other important functions such as protein folding.
Every member of this mammal family is an obligate carnivore with retractile claws and a powerful bite, from forest dwellers to desert hunters — which family is it?
Felidae is the family of mammals in the order Carnivora colloquially referred to as cats.
Co-author of 'The Communist Manifesto' and lifelong collaborator with Karl Marx, this German theorist finished the second and third volumes of 'Das Kapital' after his partner's death — who is he?
Friedrich Engels (28 November 1820 - 5 August 1895) was a German philosopher, social and political theorist, journalist, businessman, and revolutionary socialist.

Colorless, odorless, and oddly sweet, this viscous sugar alcohol carries three hydroxyl groups, forms the backbone of every triglyceride in animal fat, and moonlights as a food sweetener — what is it?
Glycerol is a sugar alcohol with chemical formula C3H5(OH)3.

Element 108's isotope 270 carries magic numbers of protons and neutrons that shore it up against fission, yet the most stable forms last only about ten seconds — which synthetic superheavy element is it?
Hassium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Hs and atomic number 108.
Running from the shoulder to the elbow, this arm bone connects the scapula to the radius and ulna, with a rounded head and neck at one end and two epicondyles at the other — name this bone?
Humerus (pl.: humeri) is a long bone in the arm that runs from the shoulder to the elbow.
Denoted by the symbol ∞, this concept of the boundless and endless has been debated by philosophers since ancient Greece and by mathematicians since the 17th century — what is it?
Infinity is something which is boundless, limitless, or endless.
This American businessman and chemist owned the Los Angeles Lakers through their 'Showtime' era of the 1980s, winning 10 league championships as majority owner. Who is he?
Jerry Buss (January 27, 1933 - February 18, 2013) was an American businessman, investor, chemist, and philanthropist.
Found from Africa to the Americas, this family of 118 bird species has big heads and sharp bills, and though most picture them by rivers, many actually live deep in forests — what are they?
Kingfisher are a family, the Alcedinidae, of small to medium-sized, brightly coloured birds in the order Coraciiformes.
This Soviet theoretical physicist laid the foundations of twentieth-century condensed matter physics and explained the theory behind superfluid helium — who is he?
Lev Landau (22 January 1908 - 1 April 1968) was a Soviet physicist who made fundamental contributions to many areas of theoretical physics.
Its name is Latin for 'wolf,' and this autoimmune disease cycles between flares and remission, often announcing itself with a red rash across the face — what is it?
Lupus (SLE), is an autoimmune disease in which the body's immune system mistakenly attacks healthy tissue in many parts of the body.
Working on the geometry of Riemann surfaces, this Tehran-born Stanford professor became in 2014 the first woman and first Iranian to win the Fields Medal — who was she?
Maryam Mirzakhani (12 May 1977 - 14 July 2017) was an Iranian mathematician and a professor of mathematics at Stanford University.
Entering Soviet service in 1983 alongside the larger Su-27, this 'Fulcrum' air-superiority fighter was later adapted into a multirole jet — which aircraft is it?
Mikoyan MiG-29 (NATO reporting name: Fulcrum) is a twin-engine fighter aircraft designed in the Soviet Union.
Lacking a cell wall entirely, this tiny bacterial species causes a form of atypical lung infection linked to cold agglutinin disease — which microbe first isolated as the 1944 'Eaton agent'?
Mycoplasma pneumoniae is a species of very small-cell bacteria that lack a cell wall, in the class Mollicutes.
A child prodigy turned MIT mathematician, this American thinker is considered the originator of cybernetics — the science of communication in living things and machines. Who was he?
Norbert Wiener (November 26, 1894 - March 18, 1964) was an American computer scientist, mathematician, and philosopher.
Derived from an ancient Roman unit called the uncia, this unit of mass equals 1/16 of a pound in its common form, though a heavier 'troy' version weighs precious metals — name the unit?
Ounce is any of several different units of mass, weight, or volume and is derived almost unchanged from the uncia, an Ancient Roman unit of measurement.
Brought on by too little niacin, this disease announces itself with the 'three D's' — dermatitis on sun-exposed skin, diarrhea, and dementia — what is it?
Pellagra is a disease caused by a lack of the vitamin niacin (vitamin B3).
What small, tailless, round-bodied mountain mammal — a close relative of the rabbit with short rounded ears — includes a large-eared Himalayan species that lives above 6,000 meters?
Pika is a small, mountain-dwelling mammal native to Asia and North America.
Legally defined as exactly 0.45359237 kilograms and divided into 16 avoirdupois ounces, this unit of mass is used in both British imperial and U.S. customary systems — what is it?
Pound (mass) is a unit of mass used in both the British imperial and United States customary systems of measurement.

The sole species in its genus within the same plant family as apples and pears, this deciduous tree produces a hard, aromatic golden-yellow fruit that's tart raw but turns into jam when cooked — name the fruit?
Quince (Cydonia oblonga) is the sole member of the genus Cydonia in the Malinae subtribe (which contains apples, pears, and other fruits) of the Rosaceae family.

This interdisciplinary field studies and practices the design, construction, and operation of robots, typically combining a power source, mechanical structure, control circuitry, and software — what's the field called?
Robotics is the interdisciplinary study and practice of the design, construction, operation, and use of robots.
This group of autoimmune diseases causes patches of thickened skin and poor blood flow to the fingers in cold weather, with one severe subtype called CREST syndrome — what condition is it?
Scleroderma is a group of autoimmune diseases that may result in changes to the skin, blood vessels, muscles, and internal organs.
This Irish mathematician and physicist held Cambridge's Lucasian chair for a record 54 years and lent his name to a theorem in vector calculus and to equations of fluid motion — who was he?
Sir George Stokes, 1st Baronet (stohks; 13 August 1819 - 1 February 1903), was an Irish mathematician and physicist.

Named in 1880 from Greek words meaning 'bunch of grapes' and 'kernel,' this genus of spherical, Gram-positive bacteria grows in grape-like clusters and can survive with or without oxygen — what's the genus called?
Staphylococcus (staphul), meaning "bunch of grapes", and (kkkos), meaning "kernel" or "Kermes", is a genus of Gram-positive bacteria in the family Staphylococcaceae from the order Bacillales.
This American singer-songwriter has won eleven Grammy Awards across folk, alternative country, and Americana, and was named one of Time's Women of the Year in 2026. Who is she?
Tagetes is a genus of 50 species of annual or perennial, mostly herbaceous plants in the family Asteraceae.
This genus of roughly 350 species of aromatic Mediterranean herbs is the source of a common culinary seasoning that shares its name — what is the genus?
Thymus (plant) (thymes) contains about 350 species of aromatic perennial herbaceous plants and subshrubs in the family Lamiaceae.
Caused by Salmonella Typhi bacteria and contracted orally, this disease presents with gradual fever, weakness, abdominal pain, and in severe cases, rose-colored skin spots. What is it?
Typhoid fever is an orally contracted disease caused by Salmonella enterica serotype Typhi bacteria, also called Salmonella Typhi.

This trailing vine of the gourd family bears a fruit that's botanically a 'pepo' — a hard-rinded berry with no internal divisions — and comes in more than 1,000 varieties, even seedless ones. What is it?
Watermelon (Citrullus lanatus) is a species of flowering plant in the family Cucurbitaceae, that has a large, edible fruit.

This paraphilia describes a sexual fixation on non-human animals, distinct from acting on such attraction, and was estimated in one 2021 study to affect about 2 percent of the population — name the term?
Zoophilia is a paraphilia in which a person experiences a sexual fixation on non-human animals.
This practice leans on 'branding' — tying a name or image to certain qualities in people's minds — to nudge them toward buying more. What field is it?
Advertising: Form of communication for marketing.
This Swedish chemist held 355 patents, invented dynamite, and then left his fortune to fund a famous set of prizes. Who was he?
Alfred Nobel: Swedish chemist and inventor (1833–1896)
Ectothermic four-limbed vertebrates whose only living members are frogs, salamanders, and the worm-like caecilians — what class of animal is this?
Amphibian: Class of ectothermic tetrapods. The origin of modern lissamphibians, which first appeared during the Early Triassic, around 250 million years ago, has long been contentious.
Designed in 1957 by a Soviet bureau and known to NATO as 'Coke,' this 50-seat twin-turboprop airliner is still license-built in China under a different name — which aircraft?
Antonov An-24: Soviet turboprop airplane. The aircraft was manufactured by the Kyiv, Irkutsk and Ulan-Ude Aviation Factories.
Most commonly caused by liver cirrhosis and its resulting high blood pressure in the portal system, this condition is the abnormal buildup of fluid in the abdominal cavity — which one?
Ascites: Abnormal build-up of fluid in the abdomen.

A North American bird of prey and sea eagle, found near large open water and old-growth forest. Its range spans most of Canada, Alaska, the contiguous U.S., and northern Mexico. This is the national bird of the United States. What is it?
Bald eagle: Bird of prey species of North America.
Native to Southeast Asia, the heart-shaped leaves of this pepper-family vine are chewed with areca nut, despite links to serious health risks — which plant?
Betel: Species of plant. Betel (Piper betle) is a species of flowering plant in the pepper family Piperaceae, native to Southeast Asia.
Launched as the 7X7 program in 1978 and designed to complement the larger 747, which American wide-body airliner first entered service with United Airlines in 1982?
Too small to fuse hydrogen but massive enough to briefly burn deuterium, these objects between 13 and 80 Jupiter masses cool over time through spectral classes M, L, T, and Y — what are they called?
With more than 220 species and over 26,000 registered cultivars, this flowering plant genus includes the very species whose leaves are processed into tea worldwide — which genus?
Camellia: Genus of flowering plants in the tea family.
A woody shrub native to South America, this starchy tuber yields tapioca and, when grated and toasted, becomes Brazil's farofa and West Africa's garri — what crop is it?
Cassava: Staple crop. Although a perennial plant, cassava is extensively cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions as an annual crop for its edible starchy tuberous root.
Known by the common name 'greater celandine,' this perennial flowering plant belongs to the poppy family and is native to Europe and western Asia — what's its scientific name?
Chelidonium majus: Species of flowering plant in the poppy family. One of two species in the genus Chelidonium, it is native to Europe and western Asia and introduced widely in North America.
Dubbed the 'father of information theory,' this polymath was the first to apply Boolean algebra to digital circuits and helped found the field of artificial intelligence — who is he?

A summer migrant to Europe and Asia that winters in Africa, this bird tricks other species into raising its young by laying eggs that mimic the host's, and even disguises itself as a hawk — what bird is it?
Common cuckoo: Species of bird. It is a brood parasite, which means it lays eggs in the nests of other bird species, particularly of dunnocks, meadow pipits, and reed warblers.

This blood-feeding parasitic insect, scientifically Pthirus pubis, typically lives in coarse body hair and diverged from a gorilla-infecting relative about 3.3 million years ago — what is it commonly called?
Crab louse: Species of insect. The crab louse or pubic louse (Pthirus pubis) is an insect that is an obligate ectoparasite of humans, feeding exclusively on blood.
This Swedish tech entrepreneur founded and chairs a streaming giant, with a net worth estimated at $8.7 billion in December 2025 — who is he?
This bodily process breaks large food molecules into water-soluble components through both mechanical action like chewing and chemical action from enzymes — what's it called?
Digestion: Biological process of breaking down food.
Sometimes nicknamed 'math dyslexia' even though it's a distinct condition, this learning disorder involves persistent difficulty understanding numbers and performing calculations — what is it called?
This stage of development begins right after fertilization, progressing from a single-celled zygote through a ball of cells called a morula — what is it called?
Embryo: Multicellular diploid eukaryote in its earliest stage of development.
This white solid is prized for binding iron and calcium ions into water-soluble complexes — handy for dissolving scale — and goes by a four-letter acronym. What is it?
This principle describes how a changing magnetic field generates an electric current, underpinning the operation of transformers, generators, and motors — what is it called?
Faraday's law of induction: Basic law of electromagnetism.
Originally focused on water, this branch of physics studies liquids, gases, and plasmas, with applications from geophysics to aerospace engineering — which field?
Fluid mechanics: Branch of physics. Fluid mechanics is the branch of physics concerned with the mechanics of fluids (liquids, gases, and plasmas) and the forces on them.
Bound together by gravity, this vast system of stars, gas, dust, and dark matter can range from a dwarf with under a thousand stars to a supergiant with a hundred trillion — what is it?
Galaxy: System of stars and interstellar matter. The word is derived from the Greek galaxias (γαλαξίας), meaning 'milky', a reference to the Milky Way galaxy that contains the Solar System.
Found in the Eastern Atlantic and the Mediterranean, this prized food fish from the porgy family is a cornerstone of European aquaculture — which fish?
Gilt-head bream: Mediterranean fish. It is a highly esteemed food fish and an important species in aquaculture.
Standing up to a meter tall with a white head marked by a black stripe to its crest, this wading bird of Europe, Asia, and Africa hunts motionless beside water — what is it?
Grey heron: Long-legged predatory wading bird.
Powered by a Rolls-Royce Avon turbojet and featuring swept wings, this 1950s RAF fighter set a world air speed record of over 727 mph in September 1953 — which aircraft?
Hawker Hunter: 1950s family of British fighter aircraft.
Overharvested in the 19th century for old-fashioned bloodletting, this European leech remains endangered in many countries today — which species?
Hirudo medicinalis: Species of annelid worm.
Marketed as Buscopan, this anticholinergic medication treats abdominal cramps, bladder and biliary spasms, and can ease respiratory secretions near the end of life — what drug is it?
Hyoscine butylbromide: Anticholinergic medication. It is also used to improve excessive respiratory secretions at the end of life.
An application of computer science, this field covers not just computers and networks but also distribution technologies like television and telephones — what is it?
Information technology: Computer-based technologies. Whisler commented that "the new technology does not yet have a single established name.

While working as an instrument maker at the University of Glasgow, this Scottish engineer's separate-condenser design transformed Newcomen's steam engine into the machine that powered the Industrial Revolution — who was he?
James Watt: Scottish inventor, engineer and chemist (1736–1819)

A Columbia economist and former World Bank chief economist who won the 2001 Nobel, he champions Georgism and skewers the "free-market fundamentalists" he blames for mismanaging globalization — who is he?
Joseph Stiglitz: American economist and Nobel Laureate (born 1943)
Also called German turnip despite not being related to true turnips, this stout cabbage cultivar can be eaten raw or cooked, stem and leaves alike — what vegetable?
Kohlrabi: Biennial cultivar of wild cabbage.
Called a 'universal genius,' this Swiss polymath founded graph theory and topology while introducing much of modern mathematical notation — who is he?
The third wide-body airliner to enter service after the 747 and DC-10, this trijet used an S-duct to route its third engine through the tail — which aircraft?

Lockheed L-1011 TriStar: American wide-body trijet airliner. The Lockheed L-1011 TriStar (pronounced "El-ten-eleven") is an American medium-to-long-range, wide-body trijet airliner built by the Lockheed Corporation.
A chemical engineer and physician who also served in the Peace Corps, she became the first African-American woman in space aboard Endeavour in 1992 — who is she?
Mae Jemison: American astronaut, doctor and engineer (born 1956)
Growing out of calculus and the study of derivatives and integrals, this branch of mathematics examines functions, spaces, and limits using methods of approximation and convergence — which field?

Mathematical analysis: Branch of mathematics. Mathematical analysis is the branch of mathematics that studies functions, spaces, and operators through quantitative methods of approximation and convergence.
This scientific field studies the atmosphere and short-term weather phenomena, with applications spanning aviation, agriculture, and disaster management — what field is it?
Meteorology: Scientific study of the atmosphere focusing on weather forecasting.
Cultivated by the Aztecs and named partly for a Mexican state capital, this flower opens each evening between four and eight o'clock and perfumes the night before closing by morning — which plant?

Mirabilis jalapa: Species of flower. Mirabilis jalapa, the marvel of Peru or four o'clock flower, is the most commonly grown ornamental species of Mirabilis plant, and is available in a range of colors.
Sold under the brand name Bactroban, this topical antibiotic treats impetigo and clears MRSA from the nose — what is it?
Derived from the Greek word for kidney, this medical specialty covers kidney function, disease, and treatments ranging from diet changes to dialysis and transplantation — which field?
Nephrology: Medical study concerned with the kidneys.

Sometimes called "radiology done inside out," this medical specialty records radiation emitted from within the body and emphasizes function over anatomy — using scans like SPECT and PET. What's the field?
Nuclear medicine: Medical specialty. Nuclear medicine (nuclear radiology) is a medical specialty involving the application of radioactive substances in the diagnosis and treatment of disease.
With atomic number 76 and symbol Os, this bluish-white transition metal has the highest density of any stable element and was once prized for fountain-pen nib tips — what is it?
Osmium: Chemical element with atomic number 76 (Os). Osmium (from Ancient Greek ὀσμή (osmḗ) 'smell') is a chemical element; it has symbol Os and atomic number 76.

Native across Europe, Asia, and Africa, this medium-sized game bird's family ties are murkier than expected — genetically, some species lean toward pheasants, others toward junglefowl. What bird is it?
Partridge: Common name for a type of bird.
Smaller than 3 millimetres and caused by leaking capillaries, these tiny red or purple skin spots can be forensically significant when found around the eyes or neck — what are they called?
Petechia: Small red or purple blemish on the skin, eyes, etc. due to rupture of capillaries.
Evergreen conifers of the genus Pinus, these trees grow their needle leaves in bunches of two to five and yield both the nuts used in pesto and the resin that flavors retsina wine?
Pine: Genus of coniferous trees. A pine is any conifer in the genus Pinus of the family Pinaceae.
Better known in the kitchen as cream of tartar, this winemaking byproduct helps stabilize egg whites for fluffier meringues — what compound is it?
Potassium bitartrate: Chemical salt used in cooking as cream of tartar.
Crossing the line between the natural and social sciences, this discipline scientifically studies the mind and behavior — both conscious and unconscious — in humans and other animals. What is it?
Psychology: Study of mental functions and behaviors.
Also marketed as canola once bred to lower its naturally high erucic acid content, this yellow-flowered Brassicaceae crop is the world's third-largest source of vegetable oil — which plant?
Rapeseed: Plant species grown for its oil-rich seed.
Its seeds yield castor oil but also harbor a highly potent toxin — which plant genus, better known for producing the castor bean?
Ricinus: Monotypic genus of plant in the spurge family.
Belonging to the order Urodela and reaching their greatest diversity in the Appalachian Mountains, these tailed, lizard-shaped amphibians never have more than four front toes — what are they?
Salamander: Order of amphibians. All ten extant salamander families are grouped together under the order Urodela, the sole surviving order from the group Caudata.
Named from Greek words meaning 'horse' and 'sea monster,' this small bony fish sports an upright posture, a curled tail, and bony armor plating — which creature is it?

Usually triggered by a viral infection and common in people with asthma or cystic fibrosis, this inflammation of the facial mucous membranes causes congestion, facial pain, and loss of smell. What condition is it?
Sinusitis: Inflammation of the sinus' membranes. Sinusitis is a condition that affects both children and adults.

Starting from stem cells near the wall of the seminiferous tubules, this multi-stage process runs cells through two rounds of meiosis to turn diploid germ cells into haploid swimmers. What is it called?
Belonging to a fish family whose fossils date back to the Late Cretaceous, these long-lived, late-maturing fish share their order with paddlefish and once swam as far as North Africa — what are they?
Pig-shaped with a short, flexible snout, this odd-toed ungulate mammal lives in the jungles of South and Central America and Southeast Asia, alongside equine and rhino relatives — which animal?
